doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: Accompanying Anita O'Day and the Brazil trip
summary: Anita O'Day ran through verses, so he asked her to name the word for each chord; he describes the Brazil tour.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: winging it. You know she was taking a slight liberty, and thank goodness I knew the tune. You know. But I mean most singers had charts and it would be, I remember Anita O’Day was a bit difficult because she would do verses and really just run right through the verse. And I wouldn’t have the words, it would be a tune I didn’t know the words to the verse. And she’d have like somebody had done a lead sheet with the melody but that’s not what she did. She was just running right through it to get to whatever it was. And so finally I just told her, like because she was screaming at me, you know like whatever. Anita would scream and I was old enough to kind of scream back. And I said, “Just tell me the word you want the chord on and I’ll be there.” You know so we actually did that. So the word whatever, okay chord here. So and then I’d catch her on the word rather than try to read this thing. And she’s running through it, and then oh we’re already in the tune you know. So yeah those were, that was one of the more difficult things, but it got resolved. Somebody just sent me, I went to Brazil with Anita O’Day and somebody just sent me an audio of it. I could send it to you. And she’s doing a lot of ballads. It’s kind of interesting, I guess it’s 1984, and she’s not in the greatest shape, you know, vocally, but there are times when it was magic, really, because the time and whatever, that was her thing. And so that was one of the more difficult gigs that I did because she was in a certain place I think in her life and then I think things got a little better for her after that.
